chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from his brother Al-Hasan from Zur'ah from Samaanah, who said:

I asked him about a man who married a young girl or enjoyed her (in temporary marriage), and a trustworthy or untrustworthy man informed him, saying, 'This is my wife,' and he had no proof. He (the Imam) said, 'If he is trustworthy, do not approach her; and if he is untrustworthy, do not accept from him.'

key_terms.ثِقَة: Trustworthy (a technical term for a reliable narrator or witness)
key_terms.جَارِيَة: Young girl or female slave, often referring to a wife in temporary marriage or concubine
key_terms.يَقْرَبْهَا: He approaches her (referring to marital relations/consummation)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling when a man claims a woman is his wife based on a witness's testimony without proof?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes a nuanced evidentiary standard in Shia jurisprudence for validating marital claims based on third-party testimony rather than formal proof. It distinguishes between a trustworthy (*thiqah*) witness, whose testimony warrants caution and temporary separation to prevent illicit relations, and an untrustworthy (*ghayr thiqah*) witness, whose testimony is rejected outright. This ruling highlights the Shia emphasis on verifying lineage and marital status to preserve family integrity, reflecting the broader legal principle of *istishab* (presumption of continuity) balanced with evidentiary rigor.
